translation_notes: g.subjects() has BOTH predicate and object free -- not the one-known-position read the stratum's short form (`for o in m{ {s} p ?o }`) covers. No island form projects a single variable while leaving two other positions as wildcards: a blank node in a pattern is a non-distinguished variable that is matched but not projected, but that is documented only for genuine blank-node positions, not as a general throwaway-variable idiom. Had to write the full triple pattern `m{ ?s ?p ?o }` and destructure `for s, _p, _o in ...`, discarding two variables to get the one the original wanted. Confirms the known gap noted in AGENT_BATCH.md: a free-predicate one-step read has no short form.

The region reads a real file from disk (output_dir, filename), not a passed-in graph, so there is no fixture= graph argument; the fixture is a real Turtle file (fixture_ok.ttl) next to the pair, plus a nonexistent filename for the os.path.isfile zero-solution branch.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: `g = rdflib.Graph(); g.parse(...)` becomes `rdflib.Graph().parse(...)` (parse returns the graph); the fallback line scan becomes a set comprehension over `map(str.strip, f)` returned from inside `with open(path)`, so `names` and its `add` loop go. The `except OSError: return set()` still covers the open and the reading, as before.

optimized.ldpy is identical to optimized.py (rule 4): the only read is `g.subjects()`, free predicate and object; its island form `for s, _p, _o in m{ ?s ?p ?o }` plus `@graph g` measured 82 tokens against 75 for `for s in g.subjects()`.
No exception to the symmetry rule.
